summary: Keyword 'character-name-in-title' is extremely selective (10 mk rows, 10 unique movies). Drive from mk CSR, intersect with US-company movies, probe cast_info, look up name LIKE 'B%'. Whole probe pipeline is tiny; only the b_prefix scan over 4.17M names is non-trivial.

resolve_constants.name: us_code
resolve_constants.method: linear scan; match exact bytes '[us]' (length 4); result is int16 dict id

filters.applied_via: direct int16 compare against us_code on cn.country_code[cid-1]
precomputed uint8 b_prefix array indexed by id-1; check 1st byte == 'B'

join_order.notes: single CSR slice; load movie_keyword/movie_id.bin and gather mk_mv[rowid] for each rowid in [lo,hi)
tiny; use std::vector + std::sort + std::unique, or a small hash set
for each candidate movie mv, iterate mc rows [mc_off[mv-1], mc_off[mv]); break on first cid whose cn_cc[cid-1]==us_code
for each surviving mv, iterate ci rows; for each person_id pid, if b_prefix[pid-1] then load n.name[pid-1] and update MIN

data_structures.b_prefix: std::vector<uint8_t> of size 4167491 (one byte per name, value = (name_off[i+1]-name_off[i] >= 1 && name_dat[name_off[i]] == 'B'))
data_structures.cn_cc: mmapped int16 array (234997) — random access by company_id-1
data_structures.mk_k_off: mmapped int32 array (134171) — CSR offsets keyed by k_id
data_structures.mk_k_row: mmapped int32 array (4523930) — CSR row ids
data_structures.mc_mv_off: mmapped int32 array (2528314) — offsets_only per movie_id
data_structures.ci_mv_off: mmapped int32 array (2528314) — offsets_only per movie_id
data_structures.min_name: std::string (held as std::string_view during scan, materialized at the end)

details: Parallelize the b_prefix build over 4.17M names using a parallel for over equal row ranges (12 threads). This is the dominant scan.
All other steps (10 movies after keyword filter) are trivially sequential — DO NOT spawn threads for them.

aggregation.implementation: Track current minimum as std::string (or std::string_view referencing mmapped name.dat). On each match, compare candidate name bytes via std::string_view::compare; replace if smaller. Both output columns (member_in_charnamed_american_movie, a1) emit the same MIN value.
aggregation.notes: Both projected columns are MIN(n.name); compute once, project twice.

memory_budget_bytes.mmap_only_arrays: no resident-set growth; OS page cache

implementation_notes: Skip all unnecessary work: do NOT materialize movie sets via hash maps — use a small sorted vector (size ~10).
Break out of mc loop on first US-company hit (semi-join).
For ci probe, do NOT break — must find min over all matching B-prefix persons.
Resolve k_id and us_code BEFORE any heavy scan; if either is not found, emit NULL/empty result and exit.
Use mmap for all *.bin files; avoid copying.
For MIN comparison, compare raw byte lengths via std::string_view to avoid std::string copies until final emit.
